body:
WHAT
Each open workspace ('tab') runs its own engine child process. Opening a workspace with saved credentials spawns it, a model change on a tab without a live child or an explicit restart re-spawns it, closing the tab or quitting kills it (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 3 s). A replacement for the same tab never starts while the previous child is still exiting.

WHY
Two engines on the same workspace race over its state files, and a child left behind on quit is a zombie holding the workspace.

WHERE
app/main.js — engineTabs Map, createTab()/closeTab()/tabForWorkspace(); startEngine(workspace, model, tabId) (calls stopEngine(tab), waits on tab.dying.once("exit") before spawning, spawn(entry.command, args, { env: { ...process.env, ...readWorkspaceEnvKeys(workspace), MAGENTRA_MODEL } })); stopEngine(tab) (child.expectedExit = true, stdin.end(), kill SIGTERM, 3000 ms SIGKILL timer, tab.dying); stopAllEngines() on "window-all-closed" and "before-quit"; engineEntryPoint() picks engine.cjs via process.execPath + ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE when packaged; the child "exit" handler emits engine_exit with `expected`; ipcMain.on("engine:restart"); openWorkspace() spawns only when hasCredentials().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. openWorkspace on a folder with credentials spawns exactly one child with args containing --serve and --cwd <workspace>, and the workspace .env keys override inherited process.env values in the child's env.
2. Calling startEngine again on the same tab while the old child has not exited does not spawn; the new spawn happens only after the old child's 'exit' event fires.
3. stopEngine sends SIGTERM immediately and SIGKILL after 3 seconds if the child is still alive; a child that exits in time clears the kill timer.
4. A deliberate stop emits engine_exit with expected:true; a child that dies on its own emits expected:false (so the renderer shows a crash banner only then).
5. before-quit and window-all-closed call stopAllEngines, leaving no tab with a live child; closeTab kills that tab's engine only.
